proofs.locator: Supplement A.3 pp.1–2; deterministic Lemmas C.3–C.5 pp.4–6; Section C.3 p.7
map: A.3: optimality inequalities and strong concavity give kappa-Lipschitz y*; Danskin identity gives grad Phi=grad_x f(x,y*) and (ell+kappa ell)-smooth Phi.

Deterministic C.3 uses smoothness, the update and Young inequality. C.4 combines projected-ascent contraction (13), motion of y*, and gradient-error control. C.5 bounds descent by -7eta_x||grad Phi||^2/16+9eta_x ell^2 delta/16.
C.3 sets gamma=1-1/(2kappa)+4kappa^3 ell^2 eta_x^2, iterates C.4 with delta0<=D^2 in (16), inserts into C.5 in (17), and sums geometric weights bounded by 4kappa.
The penultimate bound is Phi(x_N)<=Phi(x0)-(103eta_x/256)sum_(t=0)^(N-1)||grad Phi(x_t)||^2+9eta_x kappa ell^2 D^2/4, with N=T+1. The last numeric simplification is excluded.
proofs.omitted_details: Long source Proof retained as an actually read Proof map, not independently reproved. External citations in A.3 and projected-ascent contraction are source Proof inputs, not independently reviewed records.
proofs.reading_coverage: Selected deterministic passages of A.3 and C.1–C.3 read through text and corresponding registered original-page JPEGs; no stochastic Proof or whole-paper claim.

proofs.full_local_argument: Let eta=eta_x and g_t=||grad Phi(x_t)||. Since 2eta kappa ell=kappa/[8(kappa+1)^2]<=1/32<=1/16, eta/2-2eta^2 kappa ell>=7eta/16 and eta/2+2eta^2 kappa ell<=9eta/16. Thus C.5 follows at the C.1 step from deterministic C.3 and ||grad Phi-grad_x f||^2<=ell^2 delta, using the step size specified in this local calculation. For kappa>1, the read C.4 argument applies. For kappa=1, contraction (13) gives y_t=y*(x_(t-1)); Lipschitzness of y* gives delta_t<=eta^2||grad_x f(x_(t-1),y_(t-1))||^2<=2eta^2 ell^2 delta_(t-1)+2eta^2 g_(t-1)^2 <=(1/2+4ell^2 eta^2)delta_(t-1)+4eta^2 g_(t-1)^2, the C.4 recurrence at kappa=1. Now gamma>=0 and 4kappa^3 ell^2 eta^2=kappa^3/[64(kappa+1)^4]<=1/(64kappa), hence gamma<=1-1/(4kappa). Also (9eta^3 ell^2 kappa^3/4)/eta=9kappa^3/[1024(kappa+1)^4]<=9/(1024kappa). The geometric summation therefore bounds the positive gradient-feedback term by (9eta/256)sum g_t^2, leaving 7eta/16-9eta/256=103eta/256; the initial-error term is at most 9eta kappa ell^2 D^2/4. For N=1 the empty double sums vanish and the same weaker bound holds. Replace Phi(x_N) by its lower bound Phi_* and divide by 103eta N/256 to obtain the displayed average bound. Conditional on the deterministic trajectory, uniform J has expectation exactly (1/N)sum g_t^2, and the minimum is no larger than the average. Requiring this bound <=epsilon^2 gives the stated integer horizon. Since (kappa+1)^2<=4kappa^2, substitution of eta gives the Big-O. This local argument assumes the read source smoothness identity and projected-ascent contraction; it does not independently reprove the entire literature Proof.

assumptions: f:R^(m+n)->R is differentiable with globally ell-Lipschitz joint gradient in Euclidean norm; for every x, f(x,.) is mu-strongly concave.

Y is nonempty closed convex with diameter at most D and exact Euclidean projection available; x0 in R^m, y0 in Y; Phi_*>-infinity. Closedness/nonemptiness and finite lower gap are explicit well-posedness conditions; the source states convex bounded Y and writes min Phi.
statement.conclusion: E_J||grad Phi(x_J)||^2=(1/N)sum_(t=0)^(N-1)||grad Phi(x_t)||^2 <= [256 Delta/(103 eta_x)+576 kappa ell^2 D^2/103]/N. The minimum squared gradient over the same indices is also at most this bound (existence only). Thus N>=max(1,ceil((256 Delta/(103 eta_x)+576 kappa ell^2 D^2/103)/epsilon^2)) gives RMS stationarity, with N=O(1+(kappa^2 ell Delta+kappa ell^2 D^2)/epsilon^2).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean spaces R^m,R^n; Phi(x)=max_(y in Y)f(x,y); y*(x) is the unique maximizer; Phi_*=inf_(x in R^m)Phi(x), Delta=Phi(x0)-Phi_*; delta_t=||y_t-y*(x_t)||^2. eta_x=1/[16(kappa+1)^2 ell], eta_y=1/ell. For t=0,...,N-1 use simultaneous x_(t+1)=x_t-eta_x grad_x f(x_t,y_t), y_(t+1)=P_Y(y_t+eta_y grad_y f(x_t,y_t)).
statement.parameter_domains: m,n positive integers; ell>=mu>0, kappa=ell/mu>=1, D>=0, N positive integer; epsilon>0 for the stopping corollary.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible instance and initialization and every integer N>=1, the trajectory is deterministic. Independently choose J uniform on {0,...,N-1}.
